events.description: Died
Marriage

Her 10.390 shares in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B to her eight children — Lucy Nicholas, Michael, Makura, Graham, Andrew, Ken Arama, Hannah Wano, Charlie Arama (AT 12/360)

Received, by two exchange orders (HK 17/294-7), the Rotokakahi A3B1B1B shares of Arapeta and Hone Peri Paraihe, the three Okena Peri children and Ria Hone Wharewaka's five successors — consolidating Peri Paraihe's 3/7 of the block in the three Rihari Matiu children

Succession application (s 78A/67) adjourned: the Court, referring to AT 11/300-301, directed the Acting Registrar to obtain her original will from Malcolm Douglas, solicitor, Manurewa, so the succession could be completed (12 AT 232, item 62); the orders followed on 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360)

Succession application (s 78A) heard at Auckland: nine children listed as present or absent (Lucy Nicholas, Betty/Erihapeti Hori, Michael, Makura, Graham, Andrew and Ken Arama, Hannah Wano, Charlie Arama); the will not produced, only an unsigned copy — Registrar to obtain it from the solicitor (11 AT 300)

name: Betty Hori
notes: Potential false successor. On an intestacy (Wiremu Arama died without a will) every surviving child shares equally, so a sole vesting in one daughter means either she was the only survivor or the Court was not told about the others. The timing is suggestive too — fifteen years after the death, and within about a year of Rirena's death in 1980. A namesake 'Erihapeti Hori', f.a., 3.00839 shares in Tutukau East Z (Waiariki; docs 1164488 → 880411, 1972–1990), is one of six equal successors to HORI HORI (18.05035 on the 1957 title) and is NOT attributed to Betty Hori — see D016. On 1 Jul 1981 she was sworn as applicant and said 'The deceased was my father' (12 AT 232, doc 1682179); her full evidence is on folio 233. Court minutes now show the parentage directly: on 17 Nov 1980 she swore Rirena was her mother and was listed as one of nine children (11 AT 300), and on 1 Jul 1981 she swore Wiremu Arama was her father (12 AT 232). The eight siblings were therefore known to the Court when Wiremu's interests were vested in her alone in July 1981 — how that came about (consent, family arrangement, or otherwise) is what folio 12 AT 233 should show; she was in turn left out of the October 1981 orders on Rirena's estate (AT 12/360). Rirena's will, as given effect by the vesting order of 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360, doc 1355796), left her Rotokakahi, Owhata, Te Puna o Hokianga and Paihia interests to the other eight children and nothing to Betty — the mirror image of the July 1981 vesting of Wiremu Arama's interests in Betty alone.

notes:
Transcription error "Riha" is resolved on Rihari Taniora's marriage certificate (Arama Taniora's brother) as mother, "Raiha Taniora". 

Unconfirmed, Raiha Rakena or Kaumatua. Facebook page Pawarenga, Te Uri o Tai (Official page).

TE KOHANGA No. 1 (inferred, 6 Oct 2026): the "Rihipeti Arama" who succeeded to Hamiora Rungaiterangi at Ahipara in 1896 and died 17 Dec 1922 is proposed by the whānau to be this Raiha (Eliza/Elizabeth), daughter of Arama Te Patara. name: Ruhia Matiu Wiripo
other_names: Ruhia Peri Matiu; Ruhia Paura Taitimu
notes: Second wife of Peri Paraihe; mother of Hone, Okena, Pirini and Arapeta Peri Paraihe (minute book 15 HK 261). The name suggests a daughter of Matiu Wiripo — which would make her a sister of Rihari Matiu, husband of her step-daughter Maraea — but that link is not stated on the record. First name reading uncertain. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE: in Paihia 1D1E2 (doc 1284640) her three sons Arapeta, Hone and Okena hold 5.317/5.318 each, exactly matching the 5.317/5.318 held by Rihari Matiu's children Hira, Rata and Rirena — the pattern of one Matiu Wiripo interest split between a daughter (Ruhia) and a son (Rihari), then among their children. Paihia 1D1C (doc 1488165): recorded as "Ruhia Peri Matiu" — sole successor in 1929 to three children who died young (Roi 1906, Hoana 1907, Hana 1909); alive in 1940. An annotation gives a further name, Ruhia Horomona / Paura Taitimu (reading uncertain), suggesting a later marriage to a Taitimu. CONFIRMED by the 1970 Rotokakahi A3B1B1B succession to Matiu Wiripo (doc 1279339), in which her sons "Te Okena Piriparaihe" and "Hone Piriparaihe" took a line-share as his grandchildren.
source: Māori Land Court records (Pātaka Whenua) — minute book 15 HK 261, 25 Sep 1936 (doc 1650181)

name: Pirini Wiripo
notes: Owner in Paihia No 1D; died 24 November 1907 (the vesting date on the order). His interest passed solely to Matiu Wiripo by succession order at Opononi, 4 May 1910. The patronym and the sole succession suggest a brother of Matiu Wiripo (a son of Wiripo Te Moki) who died without issue — not stated on the order. Also an owner in Rotokakahi A No 3B (as "Pirini (Wiripo)"): by order at Opononi 6 May 1910 his interest there went to Matiu Wiripo 1/3, Hohepa Riki 1/3, and Reora Waru, Ritete Waipouri, Ewa Tahi and Tamati Waipouri 1/12 each (from 24 Nov 1907) — three lines of entitlement, unlike Paihia 1D where Matiu Wiripo took the whole; the Rotokakahi interest may have come through a different parent.
source: Māori Land Court records (Pātaka Whenua) — succession order, Paihia No 1D, 4 May 1910 (doc 1445102)

name: Atama Matiu
notes: Recorded as "Atama Matiu alias Okena Matiu" on the Paihia 1D1E succession schedule (doc 1488172); died 31 October 1941 (HK 24/168); trustee in 1940 for the minor successors of Pati Wharewaka. His 85.000 shares in Paihia 1D1E passed on 28 March 1952 to Toma, Mane, Takuira, Topia, Pateriki, Manuera and Iwa Atama and to the six Manihera grandchildren. Paihia 1D was Wiripo land (Pirini Wiripo → Matiu Wiripo, 1910), so Atama/Okena Matiu is a son of Matiu Wiripo: his children, as "Topia, Takuira, Pataraki, Manuera, Iwa and Mane Te Okena Matiu", succeeded to Matiu Wiripo in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B on 3 Mar 1970 (doc 1279339), alongside Rihari Matiu's children and Ruhia's Piriparaihe sons.
source: Māori Land Court records (Pātaka Whenua) — schedule of ownership orders, Paihia 1D1E (doc 1479952)

name: Hariata Rongo (Hariata Hongi Hika)
notes: Daughter of Hongi Hika and Turikatuku; sister of Hāre Hongi Hika (T016) and so aunt of Tura Hāre Hongi (T007), who married Wiremu Tangata — placed in this whakapapa by the whānau (6 Oct 2026). Educated at the Kerikeri mission girls' school; married Hōne Heke at Kerikeri in March 1837 and, after his death (1850), Arama Karaka Pī of Waimā, Hokianga; died 1894 aged about 79 (Tohu Whenua; WikiTree gives 1812–1894). Because she died in 1894 she is NOT the "Hariata Haimona" who succeeded on Te Kohanga No. 1 in Sept 1896, nor the "Hariata Hongi (Mrs Davis)" declared an owner of Pokaka (group A, beside Tura) in July 1895 — those are namesakes, probably of the next generation (a daughter of Hāre Hongi Hika or of the Otangaroa "Hare Hongi" is the obvious candidate for Mrs Davis).
source: https://tohuwhenua.nz/news-stories-travel-tips/our-stories/rongo-hongi-a-remarkable-wahine-toa-of-the-1800
